title: Evals watchdog: Console dashboard + Slack/PagerDuty alerts with dedupe
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
We need an Evals-driven quality monitoring feature surfaced in the Redwood Console that ties automated eval runs to model/config changes and sends actionable alerts into Slack and PagerDuty while avoiding alert storms via deduplication and smart throttling. This ticket scopes the product requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and monitoring SLAs for the Console-side dashboard and alert integration

Goals:
- Provide a Console Evals dashboard that shows recent eval runs, baselines, and trendline regressions per prompt-set/model/config.
- Wire eval-triggering to model/config change events (canary/rollout hooks) so teams get immediate feedback on regressions introduced by a config or model bump.
- Integrate alerts to Slack channels and PagerDuty escalation paths with configurable severity.
- Implement alert dedupe logic to collapse repeated signals for the same underlying regression fingerprint within a configurable window.
- Ensure easy triage links: direct link to eval run, diff vs baseline, sample failure cases, and a runbook link.

User stories:
- As an ML engineer, when I push a model variant to staging, I want automated evals to run and show pass/fail across baseline metrics in Console within 5 minutes.
- As a PM, when a high-severity regression is detected (metric drop > X%), I want a PagerDuty incident for on-call to investigate.
- As a platform owner, I want alerts deduped so that a single regression spike produces one incident instead of repeated duplicates across many requests.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dashboard: per-model and per-prompt-set view with metric baseline, latest run, 7d trend, percent change, and top n failing examples.
- Triggering: config/model changes in the Console trigger eval orchestration (or visible flag if customer-managed pipelines) and mark run provenance.
- Alerting: support Slack webhook config and PagerDuty service integration at org and project scopes. Alerts include model/config id, metric impacted, percent change, top failing examples link, and run link.
- Dedupe: alerts include a dedupe fingerprint (model+prompt_set+metric) and the Console will suppress repeat alerts for the same fingerprint for a default 60-minute window (configurable).
- Severity mapping: low/medium/high thresholds configurable per metric with default values defined in the docs.
- Runbook: each alert includes link to a standard runbook and an option to mute further alerts for the fingerprint for N hours.
- Observability: dashboard shows alert history and mute state; all alert deliveries are logged in tracing and match delivery success/failure metrics.

Non-goals:
- Not covering full eval execution engine rewrite (ENG tickets handle runtime). This ticket focuses on Console UX, alerting wiring, and config-level policies.

Metrics to track (product + SRE):
- Time from model/config change to first eval run (target < 5m for hosted).
- False positive rate on alerts (target < 5% in first 90 days).
- Alerts per unique regression fingerprint per week (target < 3 after tuning).
- PagerDuty escalations caused by eval alerts (baseline 0 -> measure).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Where to compute dedupe fingerprint: Console (centralized) vs eval-run service (runtime). Centralized simplifies policy UI; runtime reduces cross-service chatter. Recommend: compute sketch at eval-run service, expose fingerprint to Console.
- Default thresholds: should we ship conservative defaults and force explicit enablement for PagerDuty? Recommendation: conservative defaults with an explicit org-level opt-in for PD escalation.
- Retention of eval run artifacts and failing examples: default 90 days to manage storage and usefulness.

Rollout plan:
1) Beta: enable behind feature flag for internal orgs and a small set of pilot customers, Slack-only alerts, dedupe window default 60m.
2) Expand PD escalation in staged ramp (internal + 2 customers) after 2 weeks seed tuning.
3) General availability with UI for threshold tuning, dedupe window, and mute controls.

Risks and mitigations:
- Alert storms from noisy prompt-sets: mitigate via dedupe + configurable severity + mute controls.
- Incorrect fingerprints cause missed alerts: include deterministic fingerprint algorithm + test harness and fallback to broader fingerprinting.
- Security: alert payloads may include sample failures—sanitize PII and run security review (see dependency ENG-4160).
